purpose: Apply established modeling controls without ceremony, reserve owner questions for consequential trade-offs, and turn distinctive ideas into auditable hypotheses and out-of-sample gates.

answerPolicy.ownerPromptRule: Ask only when the choice changes the human decision contract, cost or data rights, acceptable uncertainty, release risk, or another difficult-to-reverse boundary.

foundationNotDifferentiation: injury, roster, weather, rest, and market inputs
calibration, walk-forward validation, CLV, and line shopping
noveltyStandard.distinctiveOutcome: A compact decision dossier that decomposes model-versus-market disagreement, carries unresolved scenarios through the forecast, measures edge fragility, and states what new fact or price would change the conclusion.
requiredDecisionSupport: model and market implied outcome distributions
source provenance, freshness, sample support, and applicable model diagnostics
noveltyStandard.claimPolicy: Treat differentiation as a research hypothesis until a documented landscape review and prospective user evaluation support it.

workstreams.title: Champion baseline and objective
workstreams.problem: A model cannot improve coherently until its forecast target, baseline, scoring rules, and promotion metric are fixed.
workstreams.deliverable: Leakage-safe champion benchmark with frozen targets, market baselines, and reproducible rolling-origin scorecard.

questions.prompt: Should the primary engine predict a joint home/away score distribution and derive spread, total, and moneyline probabilities from it?
questions.recommendedDefault: Yes. Use one coherent joint score distribution, then derive every mainline market from the same simulated outcomes.
questions.evidenceRequired: Rolling-origin comparison against independent spread, total, and moneyline models plus the de-vigged market baseline.

questions.prompt: Which metric decides whether a challenger is genuinely better?
questions.recommendedDefault: Pooled non-push log loss is the promotion metric; calibration, Brier score, score error, and CLV are mandatory diagnostics.
questions.evidenceRequired: Same-row champion/challenger evaluation with confidence intervals and market-level breakouts.

acceptanceGates: Every target has a written as-of timestamp and leakage boundary.
Champion and market baseline are scored on identical rolling-origin rows.
A full run reproduces the same hashes and metrics from the same snapshot.

workstreams.title: Coherent team-score distribution
workstreams.problem: Point estimates alone cannot price spreads, totals, moneylines, pushes, overtime, or correlated score outcomes.
workstreams.deliverable: Joint discrete score distribution with explicit regulation, overtime, key-score, and clock-state behavior.

questions.prompt: Which first score-distribution family should earn the right to become champion?
questions.recommendedDefault: Compare correlated negative-binomial and possession-level simulation challengers against a simple market-anchored discrete baseline.
questions.evidenceRequired: Out-of-sample score log likelihood, calibration by spread/total bucket, and derived-market log loss.

questions.prompt: How much game mechanics should version one model explicitly?
questions.recommendedDefault: Model possessions, pace, field position, touchdowns, field goals, two-point attempts, overtime rules, and end-game kneels/spikes; defer play-calling micro-simulation until it wins validation.
questions.evidenceRequired: Ablation showing each mechanism improves held-out probability or calibration rather than narrative appeal.

questions.prompt: Should a positive average edge be labeled fragile or indeterminate when reasonable unresolved scenarios reverse it or push it below the decision threshold?
questions.recommendedDefault: Yes. Keep the scenario-weighted numerical estimate visible, label disagreement rather than averaging it away, and state the condition that changes the conclusion.
questions.evidenceRequired: Forecast-time scenario definitions, calibrated scenario weights, branch-level edge and sizing calculations, and prospective stability tests.

acceptanceGates: All market probabilities come from one normalized outcome distribution.
Derived probabilities reconcile across moneyline, spread, total, push, and tie outcomes.
The challenger beats or matches the frozen baseline under the promotion gate.

workstreams.title: Live-line reliability
workstreams.problem: A partial provider board must not freeze valid games or silently mix incomplete contracts.
workstreams.deliverable: Per-game atomic snapshots, deterministic catch-up, book/market completeness, quota control, and explicit freshness.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest safe publication boundary for live odds?
questions.recommendedDefault: One game, only when BetMGM and FanDuel each contain both sides of spread, total, and moneyline; preserve the last good snapshot for incomplete games.
questions.evidenceRequired: Injected 15-of-16 provider response plus an incomplete two-way market.

acceptanceGates: Complete games publish even when another game is incomplete.
No game publishes a one-sided or one-book mainline set.
Incomplete games display a stale flag and retain their last validated prices.
Catch-up retries are idempotent and respect the 450-credit ceiling.

workstreams.title: Automation control plane
workstreams.problem: Browser visits must not mutate provider state, spend credits, or call methods rejected by the public worker.
workstreams.deliverable: Background-only imports with read-only browser health polling, run history, failure isolation, and recovery leases.

questions.prompt: Where may automatic data writes originate?
questions.recommendedDefault: Use the scheduled worker plus a deterministic server-side recovery lease. A visitor cannot choose cadence or markets, and repeated reads cannot spend twice.
questions.evidenceRequired: Route audit, method tests, scheduled-run logs, and duplicate-request simulation.

acceptanceGates: Public routes reject user-selected writes.
The browser health poll uses GET and causes no provider request.
A board navigation may claim only the already-scheduled recovery lease.
A missed or failed scheduled snapshot receives at most one deterministic recovery attempt.

workstreams.title: Current roster and depth state
workstreams.problem: Team aggregates become misleading when starters, roles, snap shares, or position groups change.
workstreams.deliverable: As-of roster, depth, participation, transaction, and starter-state snapshots linked to every forecast.

questions.prompt: Which sources may define the current depth chart and starting roles?
questions.recommendedDefault: Use official team rosters/transactions as authority and nflverse participation as evidence; treat unofficial depth charts as timestamped, lower-confidence hints.
questions.evidenceRequired: Coverage, update latency, identity resolution, and historical replay for starter changes.

questions.prompt: How should uncertain roles enter a forecast?
questions.recommendedDefault: Represent role probabilities and widen forecast uncertainty; never force a single starter when evidence is unresolved.
questions.evidenceRequired: Calibration of role probabilities and forecast intervals around late changes.

acceptanceGates: Every active player resolves to one stable identifier and team as of forecast time.
Starter and participation state cannot use post-kickoff evidence.
Missing role data widens uncertainty and is visible in provenance.

workstreams.title: Player-level contribution model
workstreams.problem: Player stats are not yet a validated bridge from role and opponent to team scoring or prop distributions.
workstreams.deliverable: Position-aware player value, usage, efficiency, matchup, and availability layers that aggregate without double counting team effects.

questions.prompt: Which player groups should enter the first validated model?
questions.recommendedDefault: Start with QB, offensive line as a unit, primary receivers, and high-volume rushers; add defense and special teams only after stable participation/value estimates exist.
questions.evidenceRequired: Position-group ablations on held-out team-score and market forecasts.

questions.prompt: How should player and team features coexist?
questions.recommendedDefault: Player inputs explain deviations from a regressed team baseline; regularize heavily and test removal to prevent double counting.
questions.evidenceRequired: Nested-model ablations, stability across seasons, and calibration under personnel changes.

acceptanceGates: All inputs are available at forecast time and linked to role certainty.
Player layers improve held-out results beyond team and market baselines.
No position group is promoted solely from in-sample fit.

workstreams.title: Public-versus-sharp evidence
workstreams.problem: Ticket and money splits are noisy vendor labels, not proof of informed action.
workstreams.deliverable: Timestamped sentiment evidence separated from sharp-price movement, with source reliability and no causal overclaim.

questions.prompt: What may the engine call sharp evidence?
questions.recommendedDefault: Only price movement at a validated sharper reference market; label ticket/money divergence as public sentiment, never as sharp certainty.
questions.evidenceRequired: Source methodology, sample size, timestamp alignment, and prospective relationship to later reference prices.

questions.prompt: Should sentiment affect the probability model?
questions.recommendedDefault: Keep it diagnostic until prospective rolling-origin tests improve calibration or log loss after controlling for current price.
questions.evidenceRequired: Incremental out-of-sample test over a price-only market baseline.

acceptanceGates: Every sentiment observation stores source, sample, method, and capture time.
The UI distinguishes public sentiment from reference-market movement.
No sentiment feature enters production without incremental prospective value.

workstreams.title: Historical market archive
workstreams.problem: Closing lines alone cannot reconstruct opener-to-close movement, forecast-time baselines, or honest CLV.
workstreams.deliverable: Licensed, point-in-time multi-book snapshots with contract identity, capture time, closing rules, and coverage metadata.

questions.prompt: Do we buy historical The Odds API snapshots or build a prospective archive first?
questions.recommendedDefault: Build the prospective archive now; evaluate paid history only if its coverage, license, and timestamp granularity support the planned validation.
questions.evidenceRequired: Coverage matrix by season/book/market, missingness audit, license review, and cost.

questions.prompt: What exactly counts as the close?
questions.recommendedDefault: The last complete two-sided quote from the named book before kickoff, with a separately stored consensus close.
questions.evidenceRequired: Replay tests for late suspensions, point changes, and absent books.

acceptanceGates: Every snapshot is immutable and keyed by provider, contract, book, and capture time.
Opening, forecast-time, entry-equivalent, and closing prices are reproducible.
Coverage gaps never masquerade as unchanged lines.

workstreams.title: Shadow season and failure testing
workstreams.problem: Backtests cannot reveal every 2026 data delay, roster ambiguity, weather miss, suspension, or operational failure.
workstreams.deliverable: Prospective shadow forecasts, frozen before games, plus replayable chaos tests and weekly calibration/CLV diagnostics.

questions.prompt: How long must a challenger run in shadow before structural promotion?
questions.recommendedDefault: At least one complete regular season for structural changes, with weekly diagnostics but no in-season feature or hyperparameter tuning.
questions.evidenceRequired: Immutable pregame forecasts, source snapshots, failure logs, calibration, log loss, Brier score, and CLV.

questions.prompt: Which failures must be rehearsed before Week 1?
questions.recommendedDefault: Partial odds, quota exhaustion, stale nflverse, unresolved player IDs, late QB changes, missing inactives, roof ambiguity, weather failure, D1 write failure, and model-gate rejection.
questions.evidenceRequired: Automated fault-injection results proving last-good preservation and explicit stale states.

acceptanceGates: Forecasts are frozen and hashed before kickoff.
No own-pick outcome enters training or tuning.
Every rehearsed failure preserves last good output and emits the correct status.

workstreams.title: Public release and operations governance
workstreams.problem: Production, public source, credentials, artifacts, and deployment history can drift or expose private state.
workstreams.deliverable: One reviewed release path that sanitizes public source, verifies artifacts, protects secrets, publishes reproducibly, and supports rollback.

questions.prompt: What should be public and what must remain deployment-only?
questions.recommendedDefault: Publish source, methodology, schemas, tests, and non-proprietary artifacts; keep credentials, D1 contents, deployment metadata, and licensed data private.
questions.evidenceRequired: Release manifest, secret scan, license inventory, and public-clone build.

questions.recommendedDefault: Lint, types, tests, production build, data-contract checks, secret scan, public-source sync, versioned deployment, and post-deploy health verification.
questions.evidenceRequired: A release report tied to exact private, public, and deployed commit/version identifiers.

acceptanceGates: No credential or personal record exists in public source or history.
Public clone passes the same verification suite.
Production version maps to an exact reviewed source commit and has a rollback target.
